senses.gloss: f. (καθέδρα) a soft seat, chair with back.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 5:5">Keth. V, 5</cite> <he>ארבע יושבת בק׳</he> (not <cite ref="A02971"><he>ארבעה</he></cite>) if the wife brought four maids, she may sit in the chair (need not do any house work).
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 4:3">Kel. IV, 3</cite> <he>כמין ק׳</he> (Mish. ed. <he>רָה …</he>) in the shape of a cathedra (with a curved or hollow back).
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 24:2">Ib. XXIV, 2</cite> <he>העשויה כק׳</he> a wagon seat formed like a cathedra.

<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:1">Lam. R. to I, 1</cite> <he>ק׳</he> (<cite ref="T00152"><he>רבתי</he></cite>) <he>בכל מקום … מציעין לו</he> wherever one of the sons of Jerusalem came to a country place, they spread for him a cathedra to sit on it, in order to hear his wisdom. Pesik. Vayḥi, p. 7ᵇ (ref. to <cite ref="I Kings 10:19">I Kings X, 19</cite>) <he>כהדא ק׳ דמשה</he> like the seat of Moses (v. Revue des Ét. Juives XXXIV, p. 99, sq.); <cite ref="Esther Rabbah 1:10">Esth. R. to I, 2</cite> <he>קדירתא דדרניש</he> (read: <he>קתידרא</he>); <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 43:4">Ex. R. s. 43</cite> <he>ק׳ עשו לו כק׳ וכ׳</he> they made for him (Moses) a seat like the scholars’ cathedra in which one sits and yet seems to be standing; a. e.—Pl. <he>קְתִדְראוֹת</he>, <he>קְתִדְרָיוֹת</he>, <cite ref="S02285"><he>קְתִיד׳</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 5:1:4">Y. Succ. V, beg. 55ᵃ</cite> <he>ושבעים ק׳ וכ׳</he> seventy gilt chairs were there (in the synagogue of Alexandria), beset with precious stones &c.; Bab.
<cite ref="Sukkah 51b:6">Succ. 51ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Sukkah 4:6">Tosef. ib. IV, 6</cite> <he>שבעים ואחת ק׳</he>. Y. Ber. VI, 10ᵈ top; a. e.
